bib.title: Design2Code: Benchmarking Multimodal Code Generation for Automated Front-End Engineering
bib.venue: arXiv v3 (cs.CL), 9 Feb 2025 (preprint as printed; v1 March 2024)

question: How well can current multimodal LLMs turn a screenshot of a real-world webpage into HTML/CSS code that renders to the same page?
hypothesis: Text-augmented prompting (giving extracted text) and self-revision prompting should improve generation over direct prompting; plainly implied that MLLMs can now handle real-world UI-to-code.
contributions: Design2Code, the first real-world benchmark of 484 manually curated webpages for screenshot-to-code
Automatic metrics: CLIP visual similarity plus block-match, text, position and color element matching, validated against human judgment
Benchmarking of commercial, open-source and finetuned MLLMs with direct, text-augmented and self-revision prompting
Design2Code-HARD (80 hard examples) and finetuned Design2Code-18B

method.summary: 484 real webpages from the C4 validation set are made stand-alone (CSS inlined, media replaced by placeholder) and rendered; MLLMs get the screenshot and must output one HTML+CSS file. Output is rendered and compared to the reference screenshot with CLIP similarity and matched-block metrics (block-match, text, position, color), plus human pairwise judgments. Models are tested with direct, text-augmented and self-revision prompts; one model (Design2Code-18B) is finetuned from CogAgent-18B with LoRA on WebSight.

datasets.name: Design2Code
datasets.split: test only; 100 sampled for human evaluation; 20 dev examples used for checkpoint selection of the finetuned model
datasets.source: C4 validation set (ODC-By, released under same licence); 127.9k scraped, 14k after auto filter, 7k randomly sampled for manual curation, 484 kept
datasets.preprocessing: strip comments, drop files over 100k GPT-2 tokens, drop image-only/text-only layouts, deduplicate; remove script/audio/iframe/map/svg, external links, href, object files; replace images/video with placeholder rick.jpg; manual curation by first two authors (75% agreement on first 200)

inference.decoding: greedy for commercial models; sampling for open-source and finetuned models
inference.temperature: 0.5 (open-source and finetuned models); greedy for commercial
inference.max_tokens: 4096 new tokens (commercial models); not stated for open-source
inference.samples: inferred: one generation per item and method (no seeds or repeats stated)
inference.prompting: direct, text-augmented (adds extracted texts), self-revision (adds reference screenshot, rendered screenshot of text-augmented output, and its code); open models with single-image input get the two screenshots concatenated into one image

other.qwen_vl_chat_and_mantis: failed to output HTML in more than 80% of cases, not reported
other.design2code_18b_finetune: LoRA rank 8 on language decoder; batch size 32; lr 1e-5; 5000 steps; 100 warmup steps; 4x NVIDIA A6000, about 2 days; best checkpoint chosen by average of automatic metrics on 20-example dev set; optimizer/precision/seed not stated
other.text_augmented_prompt: not given verbatim: extracted texts appended after the direct-prompt instruction with the screenshot (Section 3.1)

metrics.name: CLIP similarity
metrics.definition: similarity of CLIP-ViT-B/32 embeddings of reference and generated screenshots, resized to squares, with text boxes masked by Telea inpainting

metrics.name: Block-Match
metrics.definition: total size of matched blocks over total size of all blocks, including unmatched (missed or hallucinated); matching by Jonker-Volgenant on text similarity, pairs under 0.5 ignored, neighbour blocks merged

metrics.name: Text
metrics.definition: character-level Sorensen-Dice similarity of matched blocks, averaged

metrics.name: Position
metrics.definition: 1 - max(abs dx, abs dy) of normalised block centres, averaged over matched pairs

metrics.name: Color
metrics.definition: CIEDE2000 color difference of text colors in matched blocks, averaged

metrics.name: Human pairwise Win/Tie/Lose
metrics.definition: vs Gemini 1.0 Pro Vision direct prompting; 5 annotators per pair, majority (>=3) decides win/lose, else tie

baselines: Gemini 1.0 Pro Vision direct prompting (human pairwise baseline)
eval.protocol: Automatic metrics on all 484 examples; human eval on 100 sampled examples, 5 Prolific annotators each (US, 2,500 surveys completed, 98% pass rate, 60 participants in total, paid $16/hour), majority vote. Fleiss kappa 0.46 pairwise, 0.32 and 0.26 for the two direct-assessment questions. Logistic regression on metric differences (50/50 split of the 100 examples, 435 Win/Lose annotations each) predicts human preference.

availability.data: dataset released under ODC-By (same licence as C4); no URL given in text

prompts.text: You are an expert web developer who specializes in HTML and CSS. A user will provide you with a screenshot of a webpage. You need to return a single html file that uses HTML and CSS to reproduce the given website. Include all CSS code in the HTML file itself. If it involves any images, use "rick.jpg" as the placeholder. Some images on the webpage are replaced with a blue rectangle as the placeholder, use "rick.jpg" for those as well. Do not hallucinate any dependencies to external files. You do not need to include JavaScript scripts for dynamic interactions. Pay attention to things like size, text, position, and color of all the elements, as well as the overall layout. Respond with the content of the HTML+CSS file.

You are an expert web developer who specializes in HTML and CSS. I have an HTML file for implementing a webpage but it has some missing or wrong elements that are different from the original webpage. The current implementation I have is: [generated code from text-augmented prompting]. I will provide the reference webpage that I want to build as well as the rendered webpage of the current implementation. I also provide you all the texts that I want to include in the webpage here: [extracted texts from the original webpage]. Please compare the two webpages and refer to the provided text elements to be included, and revise the original HTML implementation to make it look exactly like the reference webpage. Make sure the code is syntactically correct and can render into a well-formed webpage. You can use "rick.jpg" as the placeholder image file. Pay attention to things like size, text, position, and color of all the elements, as well as the overall layout. Respond directly with the content of the new revised and improved HTML file without any extra explanations.

limits: Authors: no better prompting for complex pages yet; training directly on real webpages was unstable (too long and noisy), so finetuning used synthetic WebSight
Screenshot-only input; no Figma or sketch input
Static pages only; no interactivity, JS removed, evaluation is visual similarity only
Model comparisons are not apples-to-apples (different sizes and training data)
Human agreement is moderate to low (Fleiss kappa 0.46, 0.32, 0.26); text similarity negatively associated with human preference
Block matching imperfect for granularity differences; non-contiguous blocks not merged
Models are 2024 era (GPT-4V, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini 1.0); Gemini 1.5 could not be run on main set; no seeds or repeats reported; open models sampled at temperature 0.5
Training hardware given only for Design2Code-18B

code.snippet: match_block(r_p,g_q) = (S(r_p)+S(g_q)) / (sum_{(i,j) in M}(S(r_i)+S(g_j)) + sum_{i in U_R} S(r_i) + sum_{j in U_G} S(g_j)); match_block(R,G)=sum_{(p,q) in M} match_block(r_p,g_q)

problems: Fig 4 numbers and Table 1 values are flattened in extracted text; cell-to-row mapping inferred from order

Training block is null because trains=false was chosen for the benchmark; the Design2Code-18B finetuning details (LoRA rank 8, batch 32, lr 1e-5, 5000 steps, 100 warmup, 4x NVIDIA A6000, about 2 days, 20% of WebSight, dev set 20 examples, temp 0.5, repetition penalty 1.1) are recorded here and in results only; optimizer, precision, seed not stated
